note: Background music the client approved, with the exact timing and levels that were approved. Audio files live in assets/music/ and are NOT committed (the repo is public and these are commercial tracks); on a new machine, ask the client for the file and put it at the 'file' path. Use a track only where 'suits' fits the video, never on 'avoid'. Measured values come from the approved mix.

tyler-gone-gone.title: GONE, GONE / THANK YOU (instrumental)
tyler-gone-gone.rights: Commercial track supplied by the client. Not cleared for paid ads; business accounts may get it muted. Prefer adding it through the platform's music library when posting from a business account.
tyler-gone-gone.start_rule: The file has 103.6 ms of silence before its first hit; trimming 0.1026 s puts the first audible sample on frame 0 (the hook frame). Measured offset in the approved mix: 0.00 ms.

mix.level_rule: Before ducking, the part of the track a video uses is set to the voice's loudness minus 2.7 LU (voice -15 LUFS -> music -17.7 LUFS). That is the approved mix: its 27.3 s segment measured -14.7 LUFS, with -3 dB pre-gain. A fixed gain is not enough: the track's first 10 s are -17.9 LUFS, 3 dB quieter than the rest, so a short video would sit 9 dB under the voice instead of ~7.
mix.under_voice_rule: The bed must sit 6.7 dB under the voice WHILE THE VOICE SPEAKS (50 ms blocks with the voice above -35 dBFS; voice alone vs the bed through the identical chain), as measured on the approved Brooklyn Bridge mix. The loudness match (level_lu_vs_voice) is only the starting point: on the Montgolfier edit (dense speech) it left the bed at 4.8 dB, so mix.py measures and corrects the gain before the final render.

tyler-gone-gone.approved_in: Brooklyn Bridge -> WKC story edit (lab/edit-04, wkc_bridge_v1_music.mp4), 2026-10-17: the client asked for it to be clearly audible; -13 dB with heavy ducking was inaudible.
suits: serious but positive brand or agency promos (WKC)
calm, confident talking-head pacing; 76 BPM, a beat every 0.79 s
videos that open on a strong hook frame (the track starts on a hit)
avoid: paid ads or accounts where commercial music is not cleared
videos whose voice is quiet or busy with dialogue (the bed sits only ~7 dB under the voice)
